sanskrit: nādadīta parasvāni na gṛhṇīyād ayācitam na kiṃ cid viṣayaṃ bhuktvā spṛhayet tasya vai punaḥ
english: He should not take what belongs to others, nor accept what was not begged for; and having once enjoyed any object of sense, he should not crave it again.

sanskrit: mṛdam āpas tathāśmānaṃ patrapuṣpaphalāni ca asaṃvṛtāni gṛhṇīyāt pravṛttānīha kāryavān
english: When need arises, he may take earth, water, and stone, and leaves, flowers, and fruits that lie uncovered and freely available here.

sanskrit: na śilpajīvikāṃ jīved dvirannaṃ nota kāmayet na dveṣṭā nopadeṣṭā ca bhaveta nirupaskṛtaḥ śraddhāpūtāni bhuñjīta nimittāni vivarjayet
english: He should not live by a craftsman's trade, nor desire food twice over; he should be neither a hater nor a teacher, and remain without adornment; he should eat only what has been hallowed by faith, and shun all gain got through omens.

sanskrit: mudhāvṛttir asaktaś ca sarvabhūtair asaṃvidam kṛtvā vahniṃ cared bhaikṣyaṃ vidhūme bhuktavajjane
english: Living without contrivance, unattached, holding no covenant with any creature, he should go for alms when the fire is smokeless and the householders have already eaten.

sanskrit: vṛtte śarāvasaṃpāte bhaikṣyaṃ lipseta mokṣavit lābhe na ca prahṛṣyeta nālābhe vimanā bhavet
english: When the clatter of the serving-dishes has ceased, the knower of liberation should seek his alms; gaining them, let him not rejoice, and failing to gain them, let him not be downcast.

sanskrit: mātrāśī kālam ākāṅkṣaṃś cared bhaikṣyaṃ samāhitaḥ lābhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ necchen na bhuñjītābhipūjitaḥ abhipūjitalābhād dhi vijugupseta bhikṣukaḥ
english: Eating in measure, awaiting the proper hour, composed, he should go for alms; he should not desire a gain shared in common, nor eat as one who has been honored — for the mendicant should shrink from a gain that comes through being honored.

sanskrit: śuktāny amlāni tiktāni kaṣāyakaṭukāni ca nāsvādayīta bhuñjāno rasāṃś ca madhurāṃs tathā yātrāmātraṃ ca bhuñjīta kevalaṃ prāṇayātrikam
english: While eating he should not savor the sour, the acid, the bitter, the astringent and pungent, nor the sweet flavors either; he should eat only enough to keep going, merely to sustain the breath of life.

sanskrit: asaṃrodhena bhūtānāṃ vṛttiṃ lipseta mokṣavit na cānyam anubhikṣeta bhikṣamāṇaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: The knower of liberation should seek his livelihood without obstructing any creature, and while begging he should in no way beg following after another.

sanskrit: na saṃnikāśayed dharmaṃ vivikte virajāś caret śūnyāgāram araṇyaṃ vā vṛkṣamūlaṃ nadīṃ tathā pratiśrayārthaṃ seveta pārvatīṃ vā punar guhām
english: He should not parade his piety; free of passion, let him dwell in solitude. For shelter he may resort to an empty house, a forest, the foot of a tree, a riverbank, or again a mountain cave.

sanskrit: grāmaikarātriko grīṣme varṣāsv ekatra vā vaset adhvā sūryeṇa nirdiṣṭaḥ kīṭavac ca caren mahīm
english: In summer he should pass but a single night in a village; in the rains he may stay in one place. Let his road be the one the sun marks out, and let him roam the earth like an insect.

sanskrit: dayārthaṃ caiva bhūtānāṃ samīkṣya pṛthivīṃ caret saṃcayāṃś ca na kurvīta snehavāsaṃ ca varjayet
english: And out of compassion for living things he should look upon the ground as he walks; he should lay up no hoards, and shun any dwelling that breeds attachment.

sanskrit: pūtena cāmbhasā nityaṃ kāryaṃ kurvīta mokṣavit upaspṛśed uddhṛtābhir adbhiś ca puruṣaḥ sadā
english: The knower of liberation should always do his needful tasks with purified water; and a man should ever sip and touch with water that has been drawn up out of its source.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā brahmacaryaṃ ca satyam ārjavam eva ca akrodhaś cānasūyā ca damo nityam apaiśunam
english: Non-injury, chastity, truth, and uprightness, freedom from anger, freedom from envy, self-restraint, and a constant abstaining from slander —

sanskrit: aṣṭāsv eteṣu yuktaḥ syād vrateṣu niyatendriyaḥ apāpam aśaṭhaṃ vṛttam ajihmaṃ nityam ācaret
english: in these eight vows he should be steadfast, his senses curbed; and he should ever follow a course of conduct sinless, guileless, and straight.

sanskrit: āśīryuktāni karmāṇi hiṃsāyuktāni yāni ca lokasaṃgrahadharmaṃ ca naiva kuryān na kārayet
english: Rites bound up with self-seeking prayer, and those bound up with injury, and the dharma performed for the world's regard — these he should neither do himself nor cause others to do.

sanskrit: sarvabhāvān atikramya laghumātraḥ parivrajet samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu sthāvareṣu careṣu ca
english: Passing beyond all states of being, with the lightest of burdens let him wander forth, the same toward all creatures, the moving and the unmoving alike.

sanskrit: paraṃ nodvejayet kaṃ cin na ca kasya cid udvijet viśvāsyaḥ sarvabhūtānām agryo mokṣavid ucyate
english: He should alarm no other being, nor take alarm at any; one whom all creatures may trust is called the foremost knower of liberation.

sanskrit: anāgataṃ ca na dhyāyen nātītam anucintayet vartamānam upekṣeta kālākāṅkṣī samāhitaḥ
english: He should not brood on what has not yet come, nor dwell in thought on what is past; he should be indifferent to the present, composed, awaiting his hour.

sanskrit: na cakṣuṣā na manasā na vācā dūṣayet kva cit na pratyakṣaṃ parokṣaṃ vā kiṃ cid duṣṭaṃ samācaret
english: Neither with the eye, nor with the mind, nor with speech should he ever do harm; and whether openly or in secret he should commit no evil act.

sanskrit: indriyāṇy upasaṃhṛtya kūrmo 'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ kṣīṇendriyamanobuddhir nirīkṣeta nirindriyaḥ
english: Drawing in his senses on every side, as a tortoise draws in its limbs, with senses, mind, and intellect grown still, let him gaze inward as one beyond the senses.

sanskrit: nirdvaṃdvo nirnamaskāro niḥsvāhākāra eva ca nirmamo nirahaṃkāro niryogakṣema eva ca
english: Beyond the pairs of opposites, beyond all salutation, beyond the cry of 'svāhā,' without the sense of 'mine,' without the sense of 'I,' beyond all care for getting and keeping —

sanskrit: nirāśīḥ sarvabhūteṣu nirāsaṅgo nirāśrayaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvato mukto mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: free of expectation toward all beings, free of clinging, dependent on nothing, all-knowing, freed on every side — such a one is liberated; in this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: apāṇipādapṛṣṭhaṃ tam aśiraskam anūdaram prahīṇaguṇakarmāṇaṃ kevalaṃ vimalaṃ sthiram
english: That Self is without hand or foot or back, without head, without belly, devoid of the qualities and of action, alone, stainless, and unmoving;

sanskrit: agandharasam asparśam arūpāśabdam eva ca atvagasthy atha vāmajjam amāṃsam api caiva ha
english: without smell or taste, without touch, without form or sound; without skin or bone, without marrow, and without flesh as well —

sanskrit: niścintam avyayaṃ nityaṃ hṛdistham api nityadā sarvabhūtastham ātmānaṃ ye paśyanti na te mṛtāḥ
english: those who behold that Self — free of all care, imperishable, eternal, ever seated in the heart and abiding in all beings — they do not die.

sanskrit: na tatra kramate buddhir nendriyāṇi na devatāḥ vedā yajñāś ca lokāś ca na tapo na parākramaḥ yatra jñānavatāṃ prāptir aliṅgagrahaṇā smṛtā
english: There the intellect does not reach, nor the senses, nor the gods, nor the Vedas, the sacrifices, and the worlds, nor austerity, nor heroic effort — there, it is taught, the wise attain by a grasping that is without sign or mark.

sanskrit: tasmād aliṅgo dharmajño dharmavratam anuvrataḥ gūḍhadharmāśrito vidvān ajñātacaritaṃ caret
english: Therefore the knower of dharma, bearing no outward mark, faithful to the vow of dharma, the wise man who has taken to a hidden practice of it, should move through life with his ways unknown.

sanskrit: amūḍho mūḍharūpeṇa cared dharmam adūṣayan yathainam avamanyeran pare satatam eva hi
english: Though clear-minded, he should follow dharma in the guise of a simpleton, doing it no harm, in such a way that others will continually hold him in contempt.

sanskrit: tathāvṛttaś cared dharmaṃ satāṃ vartmāvidūṣayan yo hy evaṃ vṛttasaṃpannaḥ sa muniḥ śreṣṭha ucyate
english: So conducting himself, he should follow dharma without sullying the path of the good; for he who is endowed with such conduct is called the foremost of sages.

sanskrit: indriyāṇīndriyārthāṃś ca mahābhūtāni pañca ca manobuddhir athātmānam avyaktaṃ puruṣaṃ tathā
english: The senses and the objects of sense, the five great elements, the mind and the intellect, the self, the Unmanifest, and likewise the Person —

sanskrit: sarvam etat prasaṃkhyāya samyak saṃtyajya nirmalaḥ tataḥ svargam avāpnoti vimuktaḥ sarvabandhanaiḥ
english: having reckoned up all this, and rightly renounced it, he becomes stainless; then, freed from every bond, he attains the realm beyond.

sanskrit: etad evāntavelāyāṃ parisaṃkhyāya tattvavit dhyāyed ekāntam āsthāya mucyate 'tha nirāśrayaḥ
english: Reckoning up this very truth at the hour of his end, the knower of reality should meditate, abiding in solitude; then, dependent on nothing, he is set free.

sanskrit: nirmuktaḥ sarvasaṅgebhyo vāyur ākāśago yathā kṣīṇakośo nirātaṅkaḥ prāpnoti paramaṃ padam
english: Released from all attachments, like the wind that moves through space, his sheath worn away and free of fear, he attains the supreme abode.

sanskrit: brahmovāca saṃnyāsaṃ tapa ity āhur vṛddhā niścitadarśinaḥ brāhmaṇā brahmayonisthā jñānaṃ brahma paraṃ viduḥ
english: Brahmā said: The elders of settled vision declare that renunciation is austerity; the brāhmaṇas grounded in the source that is Brahman know knowledge to be the supreme Brahman.

sanskrit: avidūrāt paraṃ brahma vedavidyāvyapāśrayam nirdvaṃdvaṃ nirguṇaṃ nityam acintyaṃ guhyam uttamam
english: Not far off lies the supreme Brahman, the resort of the Vedic lore, beyond the pairs of opposites, without quality, eternal, unthinkable, hidden, and highest.

sanskrit: jñānena tapasā caiva dhīrāḥ paśyanti tat padam nirṇiktatamasaḥ pūtā vyutkrāntarajaso 'malāḥ
english: Through knowledge and through austerity the steadfast behold that abode, their darkness scoured away, made pure, risen above passion, and stainless.

sanskrit: tapasā kṣemam adhvānaṃ gacchanti paramaiṣiṇaḥ saṃnyāsaniratā nityaṃ ye brahmaviduṣo janāḥ
english: By austerity those who seek the highest tread the safe road — they who delight ever in renunciation, men who are the knowers of Brahman.

sanskrit: tapaḥ pradīpa ity āhur ācāro dharmasādhakaḥ jñānaṃ tv eva paraṃ vidma saṃnyāsas tapa uttamam
english: Austerity, they say, is a lamp, and right conduct accomplishes dharma; but knowledge we know to be supreme, and renunciation the highest austerity.

sanskrit: yas tu veda nirābādhaṃ jñānaṃ tattvaviniścayāt sarvabhūtastham ātmānaṃ sa sarvagatir iṣyate
english: He who, through certainty of the truth, knows the unimpeded knowledge — the Self that abides in all beings — is held to be the one whose course goes everywhere.

sanskrit: yo vidvān sahavāsaṃ ca vivāsaṃ caiva paśyati tathaivaikatvanānātve sa duḥkhāt parimucyate
english: The wise man who perceives both union and separation, and likewise oneness and manyness, is wholly freed from sorrow.

sanskrit: yo na kāmayate kiṃ cin na kiṃ cid avamanyate ihalokastha evaiṣa brahmabhūyāya kalpate
english: He who desires nothing and disdains nothing — that man, even while dwelling in this world, is fit to become one with Brahman.

sanskrit: pradhānaguṇatattvajñaḥ sarvabhūtavidhānavit nirmamo nirahaṃkāro mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: He who knows the truth of primal Nature and its qualities, who understands the ordering of all beings, without the sense of 'mine' and without the sense of 'I,' is liberated; in this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: nirdvaṃdvo nirnamaskāro niḥsvadhākāra eva ca nirguṇaṃ nityam advaṃdvaṃ praśamenaiva gacchati
english: Beyond the pairs of opposites, beyond all salutation, beyond the cry of 'svadhā,' by tranquility alone he reaches the quality-less, the eternal, the one beyond all duality.

sanskrit: hitvā guṇamayaṃ sarvaṃ karma jantuḥ śubhāśubham ubhe satyānṛte hitvā mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Forsaking all action made of the qualities, good and ill alike, and forsaking both truth and falsehood, the creature is liberated; in this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: avyaktabījaprabhavo buddhiskandhamayo mahān mahāhaṃkāraviṭapa indriyāntarakoṭaraḥ
english: Sprung from the seed of the Unmanifest, mighty, its trunk made of the intellect, with the great 'I'-principle for its boughs and the inner senses for its hollows;

sanskrit: mahābhūtaviśākhaś ca viśeṣapratiśākhavān sadāparṇaḥ sadāpuṣpaḥ śubhāśubhaphalodayaḥ ājīvaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ brahmavṛkṣaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: with the great elements for its great branches and the particulars for its lesser branches, ever in leaf, ever in flower, putting forth fruits both fair and foul — such is the eternal tree of Brahman, the sustenance of all beings.

sanskrit: etac chittvā ca bhittvā ca jñānena paramāsinā hitvā cāmaratāṃ prāpya jahyād vai mṛtyujanmanī nirmamo nirahaṃkāro mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Cutting and cleaving this tree with the supreme sword of knowledge, and forsaking it, and gaining deathlessness, one should cast off death and birth; without the sense of 'mine' and without the sense of 'I,' he is liberated; in this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: dvāv etau pakṣiṇau nityau sakhāyau cāpy acetanau etābhyāṃ tu paro yasya cetanāvān iti smṛtaḥ
english: These two birds are eternal companions, and both are without consciousness; but he who is held to be the conscious one is higher than these two.

sanskrit: acetanaḥ sattvasaṃghātayuktaḥ; sattvāt paraṃ cetayate 'ntarātmā sa kṣetrajñaḥ sattvasaṃghātabuddhir; guṇātigo mucyate mṛtyupāśāt
english: The one without consciousness is yoked to the aggregate of sattva; higher than sattva, the inner Self gives consciousness. He is the Knower of the Field, whose understanding works through the aggregate of sattva, and passing beyond the qualities, he is freed from the noose of death.

sanskrit: brahmovāca ke cid brahmamayaṃ vṛkṣaṃ ke cid brahmamayaṃ mahat ke cit puruṣam avyaktaṃ ke cit param anāmayam manyante sarvam apy etad avyaktaprabhavāvyayam
english: Brahmā said: Some hold the supreme to be the Brahman-tree, some the great Principle made of Brahman, some the Person, some the Unmanifest, some that which is beyond and free of all affliction; yet all of this springs from the Unmanifest and is imperishable.

sanskrit: ucchvāsamātram api ced yo 'ntakāle samo bhavet ātmānam upasaṃgamya so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate
english: If a man, even for the space of a single breath at the hour of his end, becomes evenminded, then having drawn near to the Self he is fit for immortality.

sanskrit: nimeṣamātram api cet saṃyamyātmānam ātmani gacchaty ātmaprasādena viduṣāṃ prāptim avyayām
english: If, even for the space of a wink, he restrains the self within the Self, then by the grace of the Self he reaches the imperishable attainment of the wise.

sanskrit: prāṇāyāmair atha prāṇān saṃyamya sa punaḥ punaḥ daśadvādaśabhir vāpi caturviṃśāt paraṃ tataḥ
english: Restraining the breaths again and again by exercises of breath-control — by ten or by twelve, and then beyond that by twenty-four —

sanskrit: evaṃ pūrvaṃ prasannātmā labhate yad yad icchati avyaktāt sattvam udriktam amṛtatvāya kalpate
english: thus, his self first made serene, he gains whatever he desires; and the sattva that has risen up out of the Unmanifest is fit to attain immortality.

sanskrit: sattvāt parataraṃ nānyat praśaṃsantīha tadvidaḥ anumānād vijānīmaḥ puruṣaṃ sattvasaṃśrayam na śakyam anyathā gantuṃ puruṣaṃ tam atho dvijāḥ
english: Those who know it praise nothing higher in this world than sattva; by inference we know the Person who has sattva for his refuge — and otherwise, O twiceborn, that Person cannot be reached.

sanskrit: kṣamā dhṛtir ahiṃsā ca samatā satyam ārjavam jñānaṃ tyāgo 'tha saṃnyāsaḥ sāttvikaṃ vṛttam iṣyate
english: Patience, steadfastness, non-injury, evenness, truth, uprightness, knowledge, relinquishment, and renunciation — this is held to be the conduct that springs from sattva.

sanskrit: etenaivānumānena manyante 'tha manīṣiṇaḥ sattvaṃ ca puruṣaś caikas tatra nāsti vicāraṇā
english: By this very inference the wise then hold that sattva and the Person are one; in this there is no debate.

sanskrit: āhur eke ca vidvāṃso ye jñāne supratiṣṭhitāḥ kṣetrajñasattvayor aikyam ity etan nopapadyate
english: But certain learned men, well established in knowledge, say: this oneness of the Knower of the Field and of sattva does not hold.

sanskrit: pṛthagbhūtas tato nityam ity etad avicāritam pṛthagbhāvaś ca vijñeyaḥ sahajaś cāpi tattvataḥ
english: That the one is forever distinct from the other — this is held beyond dispute; yet their distinctness must in truth be understood as also being innate and shared together.

sanskrit: tathaivaikatvanānātvam iṣyate viduṣāṃ nayaḥ maśakodumbare tv aikyaṃ pṛthaktvam api dṛśyate
english: And so the reasoning of the wise admits both oneness and manyness; for in the gnat and the fig there is seen both a union and a separateness.

sanskrit: matsyo yathānyaḥ syād apsu saṃprayogas tathānayoḥ saṃbandhas toyabindūnāṃ parṇe kokanadasya ca
english: As the fish is a thing apart within the waters, so is the conjunction of these two; their bond is like that of waterdrops upon the leaf of the red lotus.

sanskrit: gurur uvāca ity uktavantaṃ te viprās tadā lokapitāmaham punaḥ saṃśayam āpannāḥ papracchur dvijasattamāḥ
english: The teacher said: When the Grandsire of the world had spoken thus, those brāhmaṇas, those best of the twiceborn, fell again into doubt and put their questions to him.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ kiṃ svid eveha dharmāṇām anuṣṭheyatamaṃ smṛtam vyāhatām iva paśyāmo dharmasya vividhāṃ gatim
english: The seers said: Which among the dharmas, then, is held in this world the most worthy to be practiced? For we behold the manifold course of dharma as if it were at war with itself.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ dehād vadanty eke naitad astīti cāpare ke cit saṃśayitaṃ sarvaṃ niḥsaṃśayam athāpare
english: Some say there is a state above the body; others say it is not so. Some hold that all is a matter of doubt; others, that it is beyond doubt.

sanskrit: anityaṃ nityam ity eke nāsty astīty api cāpare ekarūpaṃ dvidhety eke vyāmiśram iti cāpare ekam eke pṛthak cānye bahutvam iti cāpare
english: Some say it is impermanent, others permanent; some that it is not, others that it is. Some say it is of a single form, others twofold, others a blending of both; some say it is one, others that it is separate, and others still that it is many.

sanskrit: manyante brāhmaṇā evaṃ prājñās tattvārthadarśinaḥ jaṭājinadharāś cānye muṇḍāḥ ke cid asaṃvṛtāḥ
english: Thus think the brāhmaṇas, wise men who behold the truth of things. Some wear matted locks and skins, others are shaven, and some go uncovered.

sanskrit: asnānaṃ ke cid icchanti snānam ity api cāpare āhāraṃ ke cid icchanti ke cic cānaśane ratāḥ
english: Some choose to forgo bathing, others to bathe; some choose to take food, while others delight in fasting.

sanskrit: karma ke cit praśaṃsanti praśāntim api cāpare deśakālāv ubhau ke cin naitad astīti cāpare ke cin mokṣaṃ praśaṃsanti ke cid bhogān pṛthagvidhān
english: Some praise action, others tranquility; some praise both place and time, while others say there is no such thing. Some extol liberation, others the enjoyments of their various kinds.

sanskrit: dhanāni ke cid icchanti nirdhanatvaṃ tathāpare upāsyasādhanaṃ tv eke naitad astīti cāpare
english: Some desire riches, others poverty; some hold that worship is the means, while others say it is not so.

sanskrit: ahiṃsāniratāś cānye ke cid dhiṃsāparāyaṇāḥ puṇyena yaśasety eke naitad astīti cāpare
english: Some are devoted to non-injury, others bent upon injury; some say that fame comes through merit, while others say it is not so.

sanskrit: sadbhāvaniratāś cānye ke cit saṃśayite sthitāḥ duḥkhād anye sukhād anye dhyānam ity apare sthitāḥ
english: Some are intent on the good and the real, others remain in a state of doubt; some hold to sorrow, some to happiness, and others rest in meditation.

sanskrit: yajñam ity apare dhīrāḥ pradānam iti cāpare sarvam eke praśaṃsanti na sarvam iti cāpare
english: Some of the steadfast say it is sacrifice, others that it is giving; some praise all of these, while others say not all of them are good.

sanskrit: tapas tv anye praśaṃsanti svādhyāyam apare janāḥ jñānaṃ saṃnyāsam ity eke svabhāvaṃ bhūtacintakāḥ
english: Others praise austerity, and some men the study of the sacred texts; some say it is knowledge and renunciation, while those who ponder the elements say it is inherent nature.

sanskrit: evaṃ vyutthāpite dharme bahudhā vipradhāvati niścayaṃ nādhigacchāmaḥ saṃmūḍhāḥ surasattama
english: Thus, when dharma is raised up and goes racing off in so many directions, we cannot reach certainty, and are bewildered, O best of the gods.

sanskrit: idaṃ śreya idaṃ śreya ity evaṃ prasthito janaḥ yo hi yasmin rato dharme sa taṃ pūjayate sadā
english: 'This is best, this is best' — so the people set forth; for whoever delights in a given dharma forever exalts that one.

sanskrit: tatra no vihatā prajñā manaś ca bahulīkṛtam etad ākhyātum icchāmaḥ śreyaḥ kim iti sattama
english: At this our understanding is confounded and our mind drawn many ways; we wish you to declare this to us — what, O best one, is the highest good?

sanskrit: ataḥ paraṃ ca yad guhyaṃ tad bhavān vaktum arhati sattvakṣetrajñayoś caiva saṃbandhaḥ kena hetunā
english: And what is yet more secret than this, that you should be pleased to tell us: by what cause is there a bond between sattva and the Knower of the Field?

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa tair viprair bhagavāṃl lokabhāvanaḥ tebhyaḥ śaśaṃsa dharmātmā yāthātathyena buddhimān
english: Thus addressed by those brāhmaṇas, the blessed Lord, the world's creator, righteous of soul and wise, declared it to them according to the very truth.

sanskrit: brahmovāca hanta vaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi yan māṃ pṛcchatha sattamāḥ samastam iha tac chrutvā samyag evāvadhāryatām
english: Brahmā said: Come now, I shall declare to you, O most excellent ones, that which you ask of me; hear it all here, and lay it rightly to heart.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā sarvabhūtānām etat kṛtyatamaṃ matam etat padam anudvignaṃ variṣṭhaṃ dharmalakṣaṇam
english: Non-injury toward all beings — this is held the most worthy thing to do; this is the untroubled state, the highest mark of dharma.
